stories.title: How to Deslopify Your AI
stories.take: The answer — how to deslopify: think first and dictate your own POV before opening the tool, state your confidence and ask for pushback, and define audience, action, length and tone upfront • Go wide: ask for 6 directions that differ in angle or structure, have the model argue for each, then pick and combine • Shepherd at planned interception points — outline, first section, draft — and run a board of AI reviewers (skeptic, target audience, expert, devil's advocate) before shipping • Keep the human parts human: teach the model your taste from your best work, keep POV and narrative architecture yours, and never send what you wouldn't read yourself

stories.title: Marvell to Acquire Lumentum in Historic $115 Billion Tech Deal
stories.take: Marvell is acquiring Lumentum in an all-stock deal — headline $115B, $102.6B on proper share counts, comfortably the largest deal of the year — doubling down on optical tech for data centers and on supporting Nvidia, which backs both • Markets balked at dilution and losing a pure-play optical bet: Marvell fell about 5.5%, Lumentum about 10.6% • Also: Anthropic's 326-page IPO S-1 carries about 96 pages of risk factors, Marriott hit an all-time high, and 95-year-old Weil Gotshal is winding down after partner defections

stories.title: Where things stand as voting winds down

stories.title: Cloud gaming works — but it's not winning
stories.take: Cloud gaming works — GeForce Now Ultimate is 'progressively amazing' and Sean Hollister has beaten a Sekiro boss on it — but reliability, not bandwidth, is the blocker: any extra hop or household download can wreck a session • Economics are worse, not better, while AI data centers bid up GPUs; a future turn could come from decommissioned AI GPUs, since 99% of games run on old hardware • App-store fees, publisher streaming rights, and Microsoft's blocked 'everything is an Xbox' phone plan keep it from winning — GTA 6 may be the watershed test

stories.title: Make groceries cheap again
stories.take: Groceries are up about 30% since the pandemic — faster than wages — but stores aren't the culprit: their margins are 1-3% versus 8-10% for a typical business, while middlemen like meat packers and egg producers make 4-12% • Two proposals: a public bulk-buying option extending the government's school/military purchasing to willing grocers, and a temporary voluntary cap on a core basket (eggs, bread, rice, milk) paired with a swipe-fee cap — worth about $100 a year to a family of four in year one, $200 in year two • Bottom line from economist Jared Bernstein: presidents have very little control over grocery prices
